think_procedure: Let me analyze the shared_buffers knob in PostgreSQL step by step: 1) shared_buffers controls the amount of memory allocated for shared memory buffers used by the database server. 2) This parameter accepts values in memory units (like KB, MB, GB) or as a number of 8KB blocks. 3) The valid range is from 128KB to system memory minus other PostgreSQL memory allocations. 4) There is no special value like -1 or 0 that fundamentally changes the behavior or disables the feature entirely. 5) Even the minimum value of 128KB still functions as a regular numerical parameter controlling buffer size. 6) The knob maintains its natural order throughout its valid range - larger values mean more shared buffer memory, smaller values mean less. 7) There are no special sentinel values that cause the knob to behave differently from its core function of controlling shared buffer memory allocation.
